risk: The public repository describes a DoD system and was not reviewed for public release
mit: Security and policy review through wing PA; remove environment details now (D1)
plain: Our design files are public and have not had a security review
plainMit: Ask Public Affairs and OPSEC to review them; stop adding network details

risk: Each wing's ISSM must approve how scripts reach its gov computers. This wing's ISSM approved paste and run in writing (12 Nov 2026); other wings start without that approval
mit: Each wing gets written ISSM approval for paste and run (this wing's approval is the precedent); signed scripts through an approved channel (D2) as an alternative
plain: Each wing's cyber security office must approve how scripts reach its work computers (approved here)
plainMit: Each wing gets its ISSM's written approval; this wing's approval shows how

risk: One maintainer, no government owner, funding or support model; if that person leaves, the tool gets no fixes or updates
mit: Name an owner and a backup person; write a support plan and an exit plan (D3)
plain: One person builds and supports it; if they leave, no one maintains it
plainMit: Name an owner and a backup person; write a support plan

risk: All flows run on the PFM's personal connections; they stop when the account closes
mit: Connection handover runbook, co-owners with their own connections, daily health check (P5)
plain: If the PFM's account closes, the automatic steps stop
plainMit: Backup person, handover steps and a daily check, starting now

risk: One personal account controls the code the wing would run
mit: Signed releases with hashes, two-person review, a government-controlled copy
plain: Someone who takes over the code account could push bad code to every wing
plainMit: Signed releases checked by two people; a government copy of the code

risk: Test results and design records sit in personal accounts; federal records law requires an official copy
mit: Official copy in DoD365; confirm the e-mail path with the CIO (D7)
plain: Some project records sit in personal accounts
plainMit: Keep an official copy in DoD365

risk: GenAI.mil terms may not allow personal data; drafts carry names and contact details
mit: Confirm the terms; remove personal details before extraction (D6)
plain: The AI tool may not be cleared for names in drafts
plainMit: Confirm the rules; remove names before the AI step

risk: Status of the work and its license are unclear; no license file
mit: JA opinion, duty memo, then a license (D4)
plain: Legal status of the work is unclear, so other wings may not be able to reuse it
plainMit: Ask the Staff Judge Advocate for an opinion

risk: Unclear whether the DoD365 authorization covers the app or whether it must be registered
mit: Ask the ISSM and CIO in writing before a second wing
plain: It is unclear whether it needs its own approval to operate
plainMit: Ask the ISSM and CIO in writing before a second wing

risk: All wings share one Default environment; one wing's install can overwrite another's
mit: Settings in lists; site address the only per-wing value; test on the tenant (P1)
plain: Installs at two wings could interfere with each other
plainMit: Each wing's settings stay in its own lists; test first

risk: 24 choices in the design were never approved; flows would hard-code them
mit: PFM confirms or removes each before flows are built
plain: Some design choices were made without the PFM's approval
plainMit: The PFM approves or removes each before building

risk: A tenant data-policy change can stop every wing's flows at once
mit: Standard connectors only; ask to be told of policy changes; preflight check

risk: Members can edit settings, mandatory coordinators and the audit log
mit: Members read only on those lists; only flows write the log (P2)

risk: Office-mailbox e-mail needs Send As rights that many PFMs cannot get
mit: Settings switch with a fallback sender (P4)

risk: Lists hold names and work e-mails; a privacy assessment may be required
mit: One central assessment that wings reuse (D5)

risk: SharePoint and Power Apps limits (5,000-item views, 12 lookups, delegation) break views or searches as data grows
mit: Index filtered columns, lookup budget test, archive the log yearly

risk: No error alerts, health check or backup beyond the recycle bin
mit: Error handling that logs and alerts; scheduled export; one restore drill

risk: No plan for actions already in progress at go-live; blank review dates would flood reminders
mit: Migration mode with no notices; required dates on import

risk: Coordinators outside the wing (NGB, state, other wings) may not open site files
mit: PDF by e-mail and the PFM records the answer

risk: The format route depends on Word and PowerShell on the gov computer; the route is not chosen yet
mit: Renderer round 2 on the gov computer decides the route

risk: Some drafts may be CUI; lists and files have no CUI marking or handling rule
mit: CUI field, banner and rule; short PFM training

risk: Canvas apps are not accessible by default (Section 508)
mit: Accessibility checker at 0 errors, screen-reader and keyboard test, statement

risk: DAFMAN 90-161 changes reach our rules only when the maintainer releases an update
mit: Rule catalog versioned to the DAFMAN edition; PFM checks each DAFMAN change

risk: No ANG-wide mandate for a publishing tool; uptake may be low
mit: Offer as an optional tool endorsed by NGB; second-wing pilot first

risk: Design work uses a commercial AI on a personal device (fake data only); policy acceptance not confirmed
mit: Written approval of the fake-data-only method from the CIO

risk: The update source sits on the maintainer's site; updates stop if that PFM leaves
mit: Host it with the product owner; co-owner on the site

risk: Flows run in UTC; date-only values can shift a day; drill weekends not modeled
mit: Time zone setting and conversion in every date step

risk: Request limits and a future premium dependency with no funding
mit: Standard connectors only; filter on the server

risk: AI-assisted formatting could be blamed for content errors
mit: Certifying and approving officials own content; human review stays in the process

risk: The design relies on rights not yet tested on the tenant (regular user, site owner, site collection admin, mailbox, environment)
mit: Rights test plan and probe flow (go.md Task 11); a fallback for each right
plain: Some features depend on access the PFM may not have
plainMit: Test every access right first; each has a fallback

risk: No higher-level sponsor: the tool stays at one wing and each wing repeats every review
mit: Gauge interest among wing PFMs first; then seek a sponsor with a concrete ask

risk: Wings copy and change the tool; copies drift apart and stop taking updates
mit: Settings in lists, not code changes; one release channel; changes come back as requests

risk: Support requests from many wings exceed one maintainer's time
mit: Named support model before more than one pilot wing; install guide and self-test reduce calls

risk: Enterprise-level reviews take longer than wing reviews
mit: Start enterprise reviews only after interest is confirmed; wings keep local reviews meanwhile
